source: due2-native (pins workflows §6.4's literal key for relation and party parts, decisions/0012, issue #56)
notes: Authored for due2; no origin result. Both rules test the same target and the same assignee, so a field the request leaves out is one completion variable that both rules read (workflows §6.4, decisions/0012): they apply together, voiding the policy, or neither applies. Either way nothing remains. Under the per-part reading that #56 replaced, each rule's part is completed alone, and the mixed completions (one rule applies, the other does not) give Permit and Deny: scenarios 1 and 2 would be Indeterminate, Deny..Permit, from combinations no request produces. Scenario 3 is the same policy with every field named.

expected.why: The request names no target, so both rules read the one variable 'target is ex:a' (§6.4): T applies both and invalid voids the policy, F applies neither. Every completion gives NotApplicable.
The request names no assignee, so both rules read the one variable 'assignee is ex:alice' (§6.4): T voids the policy under invalid, F applies neither. Every completion gives NotApplicable.
Both rules apply; under invalid a T candidate and a T prohibition void the policy, each eliminated by the other with rule invalid (§6.2), and nothing remains.
